page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 machine family. It is configured with 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor with a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. This hardware configuration consists of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates that the e2-standard-4 sits in the lower performance tiers for compute-heavy tasks. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the weak and poor categories, representing the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also reflect weak performance, with read-only large block transfers reaching 24.13 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput are positioned in the bottom 25%. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in text generation for small 135M language models, achieving 104.71 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-4 serves as a budget-friendly option for utility workloads where high-throughput compute is not a primary requirement. The dedicated CPU allocation provides more predictable performance than shared-core alternatives, though the overall resource density is modest. This instance is best suited for general-purpose applications, lightweight web serving, small-scale Redis deployments, and basic background processing tasks that fit within a 16 GB memory footprint.
